A 37-year-old woman presented to the outpatient department

attribution_limitations: The abstract says the patient was treated with oral spironolactone 50 mg/day and improved within one month, whereas the case presentation, Figure 4 caption and discussion say oral eplerenone 50 mg once daily with improvement within two months and resolution at three months. The drug identity conflicts; the abstract's one-month timing is tied to the spironolactone claim and is not repeated in the case text.
The two- and three-month visual acuity values do not name the eye; only the baseline and six-month values state the right eye.

The Brain MRI was advised and declined in the case presentation, while the discussion says MRI and detailed endocrinological evaluation could not be performed. The endocrinology referral is stated as made, but the detailed endocrinological evaluation is said not to have been performed.

claims.text: A 37-year-old woman with short stature (height 3.5 feet) presented to the outpatient department with gradual, progressive, painless loss of vision in the right eye for the past three months. She denied systemic illnesses, previous ocular complaints and medication use, and no other family member had similar features. Visual acuity was 1/60 right and 6/18 left.

claims.text: Examination showed intraocular pressure of 17 mmHg in both eyes, early bilateral posterior subcapsular cataracts, subretinal fluid at the macula and a shallow exudative retinal detachment in the right eye, with a normal left fundus; a provisional diagnosis of exudative retinal detachment secondary to central serous chorioretinopathy was made. OCT, angiography and B-scan ultrasonography supported the findings, and cortisol, growth hormone, prolactin and electrolytes were normal.
